newsitem.title: USA: Dole won't "jump off building" if loses election.
newsitem.headline: Dole won't "jump off building" if loses election.

text.p: Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole, trailing President Bill Clinton in the polls, said on Monday he expected to take the blame if he lost the election, but promised not to "jump off a building."
In an interview with CNN, Dole repeated his criticism that the media was biased in favor of Democrats and said he did not talk very often with vice presidential running mate Jack Kemp.
"It will either be one way or the other, but I'm not going to jump off a building -- jump or go over the cliff," Dole said, adding he was making the best effort he could.

Asked if his staff had served him well, Dole said: "My view is you don't look back and say, well it is their fault." He said he had been around long enough to know the outcome would be judged the candidate's fault.
He said he and Kemp "don't talk together a lot" but denied their relationship had ever been strained. Kemp and Dole campaigned together in California on Monday afternoon.
Dole also repeated his criticism that the media had a "liberal tilt" and said the New York Times favored Democrats.
"Let's face it, I think there's an honest feeling that the media ... there is a little tilt to the left, liberal tilt," Dole said in an interview on CNN's "Inside Politics" program.
He said the New York Times, which endorsed Clinton on Sunday, "might as well be a member of the Democratic Party."

In other bad news for Dole, former top consultant Don Sipple let loose in a stinging interview with Newsweek, charging that Dole "is not a man of this time," that he thought the presidency was a reward system and saying he would not make a good president.

Dole communications director John Buckley said in a statement: "For Don Sipple to criticize Bob Dole one week before the election is contemptible. His attack should be a lesson to Mr. Sipple's future clients ... if he has any."
